item.title: Ab initio exploration of hydrogen-intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides: From identifying stable structures to emergent superconductivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.00271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a first-principles study of hydrogen-intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), examining the structural, thermodynamic, electronic and superconducting properties of distinct intercalation configurations. In most configurations, the two intercalated hydrogen atoms contribute two electrons per unit cell, creating a band gap and thus rendering the system semiconducting. Among the dynamically stable configurations there is one exception to this rule, with inherently metallic behavior. The pristine phases of these materials are known to exhibit a charge density wave instability, which is fully suppressed by specific hydrogen configurations. Moreover, the semiconducting structures can be metallized by hole doping, albeit that the superconducting critical temperatures ($T_c$) are vanishingly low. On the other hand, electron doping drives the $T_c$ up to 25 K, by populating dense states above the gap. This finding can motivate further experimental exploration of superconductivity in hydrogen-intercalated TMDs through ionic-liquid gating or alkali co-intercalation.
item.dc:creator: William Wenborn, Jonas Bekaert

item.title: Effect of Rapid Thermal Annealing on the Superconductivity of ALD-Grown TiN thin films
item.description: arXiv:2611.00424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Titanium nitride (TiN) is a promising superconducting material for scalable quantum technologies owing to its tunable kinetic inductance and compatibility with CMOS thin-film processing. However, the superconducting performance of atomic-layer-deposited TiN can be degraded by oxygen incorporation, off-stoichiometry, and crystallographic disorder. In this work, we investigate rapid thermal annealing (RTA) in high-purity nitrogen as a post-deposition strategy to improve polycrystalline TiN films grown by RF-biased plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. Grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction reveals reduced peak broadening, a smaller lattice parameter, and a stronger (111) preferred orientation with increasing annealing temperature. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling shows reduced oxygen-related bonding and a shift toward a Ti--N-dominated chemical environment after annealing. These structural and chemical changes result in a 25% increase in the superconducting transition temperature and a significant narrowing of the transition width. Annealing also reduced the sheet resistance and the estimated sheet kinetic inductance, increased the residual resistance ratio, and improved the magnetic-field tolerance. Together, the structural, chemical, and transport results are consistent with reduced material disorder and improved superconducting uniformity. Because RTA is a relatively low thermal budget and is a semiconductor fabrication compatible process, it offers a practical route to improve the quality of ALD-grown TiN for superconducting applications.
item.dc:creator: Z. Sadirkhanov, A. Tuigynbek, M. Surendran, A. Jakyp, L. Akisheva, A. T. Hammack, A. B. Tikhonov, A. Kemelbay

item.title: Nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity driven by charge fluctuations in monolayer FeSe on SrTiO$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monolayer FeSe and Fe(Te,Se) grown on SrTiO$_3$ exhibit some of the highest superconducting transition temperatures among iron-based superconductors, yet their pairing mechanism and symmetry remain elusive. Motivated by the recent surprising discovery of nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM) [T. Wei et al., arXiv:2610.38421 (2026)], we investigate superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO$3$ (1L-FeSe/STO) within an extended Hubbard model incorporating both onsite and intersite Coulomb interactions among Fe $3d$ and Se $4p$ orbitals. We show that Fe-Se intersite Coulomb repulsion strongly enhances small-momentum $p$-$d$ charge-transfer fluctuations, which mediate attractive intraorbital spin-singlet pairing interactions. These electronic fluctuations may be further enhanced by forward-scattering optical phonons of the SrTiO$3$ substrate. The resulting intrapocket attraction, together with residual repulsive interpocket interactions, stabilizes a mirror-odd, nodeless $B_{1g}$ ($d$-wave) superconducting state with opposite gap signs on the two electron pockets. Both Fe $t_{2g}$ and Se $4p$ orbitals contribute substantially to this multiorbital superconductivity. The calculated superconducting gap and density of states exhibit a two-peak structure, while the Josephson tunneling conductance displays a half-lattice-period modulation, in excellent agreement with experimental observations. Our results establish electronic charge-transfer fluctuations as a viable pairing mechanism for unconventional nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/STO.
item.dc:creator: Jin-Wei Dong, Sen Zhou, Jian Wang, Gang Su, Ziqiang Wang

item.title: Three-Dimensional FDTD Simulation of Superconducting Terahertz Emitters Using an Effective Medium Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2611.00840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compact and tunable terahertz (THz) sources with controllable polarization are sought for high-speed links, spectroscopy, and imaging. In superconducting THz emitters based on a cuprate Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$, which have the potential to satisfy such properties, modeling often relies on heavy nonlinear solvers or empirical isotropic dielectrics, obscuring anisotropy, plasma response, and bias dependence. We derive an anisotropic, dispersive effective permittivity from the Lawrence-Doniach model for a layered superconductor and implement it as a user-defined material in a commercial Finite-difference Time-domain (FDTD) solver. Simulations of two device geometries reproduce linearly polarized emission from a rectangular mesa and low-axial-ratio (near-circular) emission from a truncated square mesa. This CAD-ready workflow links superconducting theory to device design, enabling rapid searches and parameter optimization for next-generation THz sources.
item.dc:creator: Ryota Kobayashi, Itsuhiro Kakeya

item.title: Direct imaging of the Ni $e_g$ hole orbitals in the bilayer nickelate La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$
item.description: arXiv:2611.01118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Models of unconventional superconductivity in cuprates and nickelates depend sensitively on the distribution of valence electrons among the $d$ orbitals. But accurately determining the orbital electron or hole occupations in these systems remains a difficult and unresolved task. Here, using $s$-core-level non-resonant inelastic x-ray scattering at the Ni $M_1$ edge, we determine the angular distribution of the Ni $3d$ holes in a single crystal of La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$. Our results demonstrate that the hole occupation ratio $\hz/\hx = 0.94\pm0.06$, thus significantly above the expected value of $2/3$ for a filled $d_{z^2}$ orbitals models and close to value expected in a Hund's-coupling picture. Our results support superconductivity scenarios in which both $e_g$ orbitals contribute to the electron-pairing mechanism in La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Sa\"iman, Feiyu Li, Junjie Zhang, Jean-Pascal Rueff, Victor Bal\'edent

item.title: Theoretical Prediction of Superconducting 2D Hydrogenated Janus V2CSH and Nb2CSH MXenes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two dimensional hydrogenated Janus MXenes represent a new frontier in superconducting materials, where asymmetric surface terminations enable tunable electronic and vibrational properties. In this work, we present the first comparative study of hydrogen or sulfur terminated V2CSH and Nb2CSH monolayers using density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory. Both compounds are structurally and thermally stable, exhibiting isotropic in plane elasticity and nonmagnetic multiband metallic states dominated by transition metal d orbitals. The asymmetric S or H terminations generate nonequivalent surface potentials and intrinsic out of plane dipoles. Electron phonon coupling constants of 0.39 (V2CSH) and 0.53 (Nb2CSH) yield superconducting transition temperatures of 2.36 K and 5.27 K, respectively, within the Allen Dynes framework. Low energy lattice vibrations, primarily involving metal and sulfur atoms, account for 77% of the coupling in both MXenes. These findings establish metal substitution as a design principle for tuning superconductivity in Janus MXenes and highlight Nb2CSH as a promising candidate for low temperature superconducting applications.
item.dc:creator: Jubair Hossan Abir, M. R. U. S. Shapon, Md. Sharear Aman, Md. Kamrul Hassan, A. K. M. Azharul Islam, Saleh Hasan Naqib

item.title: Asymmetric Little--Parks Oscillations as a Probe of Coupled Pairing Channels in Surface-Superconducting \texorpdfstring{PtBi$_2$}{PtBi2}
item.description: arXiv:2611.01764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the recent discovery of unconventional surface superconductivity in PtBi$_{2}$, we theoretically study its signatures in the Little-Parks oscillations of a narrow ring made from the same material. Using a Ginzburg-Landau model with three coupled pairing channels allowed by the trigonal crystal symmetry, we show that a fixed in-plane magnetic field can make the mean-field transition temperature asymmetric under reversal of the normal flux through the ring, while preserving periodicity in the superconducting flux quantum. The leading weak-field contribution to this asymmetry is cubic in the in-plane field strength. The flux-odd component respects the threefold crystal symmetry and changes sign when the in-plane field is rotated by $\pi/3$ at fixed magnitude. Within the homogeneous ring model, this asymmetry is absent for a single pairing channel and arises from the coupling between the three channels. Our calculations further show that increasing the in-plane magnetic field can enhance the superconducting nucleation temperature through mixing of pairing channels, illustrating magnetic control of multicomponent superconductivity in mesoscopic rings. Little-Parks interferometry with independent control of flux and field direction thus offers a mesoscopic probe of the pairing state, complementary to spectroscopic studies of the gap structure.
item.dc:creator: Yuriy Yerin, Stefan-Ludwig Drechsler, Carsten Timm, Jeroen van den Brink

item.title: Imaging the Current Distribution in Superconducting Transition-Edge Sensors with Scanning SQUID Microscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.02352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transition-edge sensors (TESs) exploit the resistive transition of a superconductor to detect minute changes in temperature. While significant progress has been made in understanding the temperature- and current-dependent resistive transition in these devices, important aspects of TES behavior under bias remain unresolved. In particular, existing TES models largely neglect spatial variations in the superconducting state and current distribution arising from device geometry and proximity effects associated with the superconducting leads and normal metal features. Using scanning superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) microscopy (SSM), we directly image local superconducting properties and transport current in two molybdenum-gold (MoAu) X-ray TES designs. We measure the local diamagnetic response to identify superconducting regions in devices voltage-biased within the transition and the Oersted field generated by the transport current to reconstruct the corresponding current distribution. We observe bias-dependent reconfigurations of the current distribution that track current-induced changes in superconducting regions, highlighting the importance of mesoscale spatial variations for TES device physics, operation, and design.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Walker, Austin Kaczmarek, Douglas A. Bennett, Jason E. Austermann, W. Bertrand Doriese, Shannon M. Duff, Johannes Hubmayr, Kelsey M. Morgan, Daniel R. Schmidt, Daniel S. Swetz, Joel N. Ullom, Joel Weber, Michael D. Niemack, Katja C. Nowack

item.title: Observation of Superconductivity in a Cu-Rich High-Entropy Alloy
item.description: arXiv:2611.02469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Cu-rich multielement alloy containing Zn, Sn, Ag, and Au was synthesized and studied to explore its structural and physical properties. The alloy was prepared by vacuum-sealed melting of high-purity elements followed by rapid quenching in cold water. Powder X-ray diffraction confirms that the alloy crystallizes in a face-centered cubic (fcc) Cu-type structure. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping show uniform distribution of all constituent elements. Magnetic measurements indicate the appearance of a superconducting transition at low temperature, while electrical resistivity remains metallic without reaching zero resistance. This difference between magnetic and transport behaviour suggests that the superconducting state may be limited to local or partial regions within the sample. These findings indicate that the Cu-rich multielement alloy exhibits unusual low-temperature properties and may represent a new class of compositionally complex Cu-based materials with superconducting characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Arumugam Sonachalam

item.title: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.02841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.
item.dc:creator: M. Cristina Diamantini, Carlo A. Trugenberger

item.title: Acoustic damping limits superfluid helium as a thermal bath for mechanical resonators
item.description: arXiv:2611.03405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermalization is a persistent problem for cryogenic mechanical resonators. The weak supports used to obtain high mechanical quality factors are also poor thermal links, while the optical or microwave fields used for readout and control can heat the resonator above the cryostat temperature. Superfluid helium is therefore an appealing exchange medium: it has excellent low-temperature thermal transport and an inviscid superfluid component, suggesting cooling of mechanical devices without the damping associated with an ordinary fluid. Here we test this idea by immersing a \qty{250}{\micro\meter}-diameter yttrium iron garnet sphere in liquid \textsuperscript{4}He and reading out a \(\sim\qty{12.47}{\mega\hertz}\) mechanical mode using cavity magnomechanics. The mechanical linewidth increases from \qty{6.1}{\hertz} in vacuum to \qty{9.1}{\kilo\hertz} after filling the cavity with liquid helium in the normal state, and reaches \qty{17.5}{\kilo\hertz} deep in the superfluid at \qty{84}{\milli\kelvin}. Thus the mechanical quality factor is reduced by more than three orders of magnitude, and crossing into the superfluid does not recover low dissipation. At the same time, the magnon linewidth remains strongly dependent on microwave power at the lowest temperatures, showing that the sphere is not perfectly anchored to the cryostat despite the large mechanical damping. The result follows from acoustic radiation: the surface motion of the sphere efficiently launches gapless longitudinal sound into the liquid, and a radiation-impedance estimate gives a linewidth of order \qty{25}{\kilo\hertz}. Superfluid helium is therefore not a low-loss thermal bath for mechanical modes that efficiently radiate compression waves. Shear motion, on the other hand, may provide a route around this limitation.
item.dc:creator: Yunhu Huang, Mehri Ebrahimi, Alireza Rashedi, John P. Davis

item.title: Superconductivity of bilayer two-orbital Hubbard model for La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ under high pressure
item.description: arXiv:2511.01801v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By combining density functional theory (DFT) and density matrix renormalization group calculations, we investigate the unusual pressure dependence of superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) in the nickelate superconductor La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$. Using the hopping integrals and on-site potentials obtained by fitting the DFT band structures, we map a quantum phase diagram of a bilayer two-orbital Hubbard model with increasing pressure in a ladder geometry, which has an intermediate Hubbard repulsion and a Hund's coupling. Near $3/8$ filling, we find a strong spin density wave order, which at $3/8$ filling shows a real-space spin pattern similar to the spin-charge stripe order along a lattice direction. At $21/64$ filling, we find a superconducting phase with interlayer superconductivity (SC) in both the $d_{z^2}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals, as well as in-plane SC in the $d_{z^2}$ orbital. Intriguingly, the SC is weakened with increasing pressure and transits to a Luttinger liquid above $80$ GPa, which qualitatively agrees with the experimental observations of decreasing $T_c$ with increasing pressure and a transition to Fermi liquid above $80$ GPa in La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$. Through a comparative study, we further show that the ratio of interaction to hopping integral, which reduces moderately with increasing pressure, may play a dominant role in the weakening of SC. Our results of this experimentally relevant model not only find a robust SC through suppressing the competing spin density wave order, but also give new insight into the unusual pressure dependence of SC in La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Yang Chen, Cui-Qun Chen, Meng Wang, Shou-Shu Gong, Dao-Xin Yao

item.title: Multiterminal Quasiballistic Josephson Effect in Monocrystalline Gold
item.description: arXiv:2512.00409v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report on the realization of a planar, quasiballistic Josephson junction array using a Au micron-sized single crystal. The system exhibits a nonlocal, multiterminal Josephson effect, where the supercurrent between any two superconducting leads is governed by the phase coherence across the entire crystal. Key evidence includes a nonmonotonic dependence of the critical current on junction length and magnetic interference patterns with periods corresponding to the shared normal-metal area. Nonlocal transport measurements further confirm that the supercurrent between two electrodes depends on the phase configuration of all the others. Our results, supported by a developed theoretical model, establish a platform for exploring complex superconducting phenomena in multiterminal ballistic systems.
item.dc:creator: K. B. Polevoy, G. A. Bobkov, D. S. Kalashnikov, A. G. Shishkin, I. V. Trofimov, A. M. Bobkov, E. A. Sedov, E. A. Krivko, M. A. Tarkhov, I. V. Bobkova, V. S. Stolyarov

item.title: Theory of planar quasiballistic Josephson junctions
item.description: arXiv:2512.00411v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a theoretical framework for planar quasiballistic Josephson junctions, where multiple superconducting leads are coupled through a large, nearly ballistic normal metal crystal. Our approach, based on quasiclassical Eilenberger equations, accounts for the dominant role of electron reflections from the crystal surfaces or single impurities, a mechanism distinct from both purely ballistic and diffusive limits. We calculate the critical current between superconducting leads for various geometries, examining its dependence on temperature and magnetic field. Crucially, we demonstrate that in multiterminal setups, the junctions are not independent but form a strongly coupled system. The theory successfully explains key experimental observations from a companion work [Polevoy et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166001 (2026)], including a non-monotonic dependence of the critical current on the interlayer length, providing a foundation for designing and understanding complex multi-terminal Josephson systems.
item.dc:creator: G. A. Bobkov, I. V. Bobkova, A. M. Bobkov, K. B. Polevoy, V. S. Stolyarov

item.title: Nonintegral Flux Trapping in Frustrated Josephson Networks of Triplet Superconductors
item.description: arXiv:2604.24734v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a Josephson junction network, anisotropic coupling between spin triplet pairing correlations can lead to frustrated $d$ vector textures that support spontaneous Josephson currents and nonintegral flux trapping. Such networks can appear in superconducting polycrystals, as well as single-crystal superconductors. In analogy to classical spin systems, in which the presence of geometric frustration and anisotropic superexchange can lead to nontrivial spin textures, Josephson networks with anisotropic Josephson couplings cannot simultaneously optimize their $\mathrm{U}(1)$ superconducting phase differences and relative $d$ vector orientations. The internal pairing structure of Cooper pairs twists as they tunnel across the Josephson junction, and the $d$ vector texture enters as an emergent geometric phase which can spontaneously trap fractional flux. For real-valued Josephson couplings between unitary $d$ vectors, the emergent geometric phase reduces to a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ structure, allowing for spontaneous $\pi$-flux trapping above a critical antisymmetric coupling, distinct from usual half-quantum vortices. Further, we demonstrate a continuously tunable nonintegral flux for complex Josephson couplings. The results of this work reveal new routes to engineer frustrated Josephson networks from the interplay of magnetic textures and spin triplet superconducting pairing order.
item.dc:creator: Grayson R. Frazier, Colton Lelievre, Yi Li

item.title: Quantum phase fluctuations quench chiral superconductivity in twisted overdoped cuprate bilayers
item.description: arXiv:2607.00630v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Twisted cuprate bilayers have been proposed to host chiral superconductivity at temperatures comparable to their large pairing scale, yet experimental signatures of broken time-reversal symmetry remain unclear. We show that quantum phase fluctuations strongly suppress chiral order in twisted overdoped cuprate bilayers despite robust intralayer pairing. At a $45^\circ$ twist, we analytically demonstrate that the chiral transition temperature obeys $T_\chi\propto t^4$ when the single-electron interlayer tunneling amplitude $t$ is weak. This collapse originates from competition between the small Josephson energy scale supporting chirality and the temperature-dependent collective zero-point energy. Chirality consequently survives only in a narrow angular window at ultralow temperatures, with relative-phase plasma softening above the chiral transition. A distinct transport signature arising from the quantum phase fluctuations is a pronounced low-temperature enhancement of the critical current near a magic angle. These findings separate pairing and chiral ordering scales and offer a possible explanation for the difficulty of observing robust chiral superconductivity in twisted cuprates.
item.dc:creator: Yin Shi, Mengxian Zhao, Fei Yang, Miao Liu, Sheng Meng

item.title: Imaging phase winding in topological superconductors with a fork-tip Josephson STM
item.description: arXiv:2609.38174v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The topological phase winding in a chiral superconductor remains challenging to access by conventional real-space probes. We propose a scheme to probe this winding with a fork-tip Josephson STM near an impurity, where two superconducting tips form an interferometer sensitive to phase differences between two positions. The phase winding remains accessible via the fork-tip critical current even if the relative phase between the fork-tip and sample fluctuates, establishing a route towards a local phase-sensitive STM probe of topological superconductivity. We numerically compute the interference pattern to demonstrate that the magnitude and phase of the order parameter can be reconstructed as a function of angle, providing a route towards resolving the longstanding open experimental problem of directly detecting phase winding in topological superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Vladislav Poliakov, Archisman Panigrahi

item.title: Large superconducting diode effect indicates nonuniform triplet pairing in UTe2
item.description: arXiv:2610.36332v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is characterized by unequal critical current magnitudes for opposite-polarity current flow, owing to broken spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries. For a superconducting pair wavefunction to spontaneously break inversion symmetry implies the formation of Cooper pairs with nonzero momentum, yielding a nonuniform superconducting state. For singlet superconductors, the formation of such a (FFLO) state has long been understood to provide an escape from high field Pauli pair-breaking -- how and why such an effect might occur for equal spin pairing is an open question. Here we report the observation of a large SDE in bulk specimens of the three-dimensional heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe$_2$, with a peak diode efficiency of 33% at the high magnetic field strength of 33.6 T, representing the highest-field observation of the SDE to date. Crucially, this nonreciprocal transport is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state near a first-order metamagnetic phase boundary. The absence of the SDE away from this slender phase-intersection argues strongly against purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries. Instead, our findings indicate spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing. We model this behavior using a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theory, demonstrating that the intertwining of magnetic and triplet superconducting orders can stabilize an odd-parity FFLO state.
item.dc:creator: Zheyu Wu, Daniel Shaffer, Dmitry V. Chichinadze, Mengmeng Long, Hanyi Chen, Andrej Cabala, Theodore I. Weinberger, Maurice Bal, Steffen Wiedmann, Dave Graf, Vladimir Sechovsk\'y, Michal Vali\v{s}ka, F. Malte Grosche, Alex Levchenko, Alexander G. Eaton

item.title: Nano-Nb Superconducting 3D Josephson Junctions Arrays in Cu-Normal Matrix: Superconducting Phase Coherence and Quantum Fluctuations Properties
item.description: arXiv:2610.36482v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the superconducting behavior, phase coherence, and quantum fluctuation properties of three-dimensional arrays of nanometric Nb Josephson junctions embedded in a normal Cu matrix ($\text{Cu-}x\text{ wt}\%\text{Nb}$, $x = 3, 5, 15,$ and $20$), with emphasis on the $5$ and $15$ compositions. Magnetic properties were measured by dc magnetization as a function of temperature and magnetic field using a SQUID magnetometer and by ac susceptibility. Transport properties, including magnetoresistance, $V(I)$ curves, and the critical current $I_c(H,T)$, were measured at fields up to $90\text{ kOe}$. A micro-Hall sensor with ten transverse voltage bridges ($5.0 \times 0.2 \times 0.01\text{ }\mu\text{m}^3$) was used to calibrate the magnetic field actually applied to the sample. Magnetization and transport measurements reveal a double superconducting transition that depends on the applied field and current: $T_c(H)$, with $T_c(0) = 8.2\text{ K}$, is associated with the intragranular response of the Nb grains, whereas the lower $T_c(H)$ is associated with Josephson coupling between grains through the Cu matrix. The response combines that of bulk Nb with signatures of weakly coupled grains, consistent with a collection of superconducting grains embedded in a nonsuperconducting matrix. The characteristic fields $H_{c1} = 400.03\text{ Oe}$ and $H_{c2} = 15\text{ kOe}$ (grains), and $H_{c1j} = 99.93\text{ Oe}$ and $H_{c2j} = 199.25\text{ Oe}$ (intergranular coupling), were determined. The critical current $I_c(H,T)$ exhibits a central maximum at low fields, followed by a long tail and small oscillations with a period of $\Delta H \approx 24\text{ Oe}$, attributed to quantum interference between coupled grains. At higher fields, magnetic flux gradients destroy phase coherence and randomize the phase $\theta$ of the order parameter $\psi = |\psi|e^{i\theta}$, suppressing the oscillations.
item.dc:creator: R. L. de Almeida, J. Albino Aguiar, C. A. C. Passos, S. K. Sharma, J. A. H. Coaquira

item.title: BCS superconductivity in the presence of wave dark matter
item.description: arXiv:2509.22892v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As particle physics and condensed matter physics continue to expand their boundaries, emerging intersections between the two fields suggest well-motivated frontiers for physics models. In particular, dark matter, which is cosmologically predicted to form the background to our ordinary matter, can affect the physics of materials in a fundamental sense. In this work, we investigate the scenario in which relic ultralight wave dark matter alters the superconductor Hamiltonian via a sinusoidal source term. The Yukawa interaction with the scalar dark matter changes the effective electron mass, inducing periodic perturbations of macroscopic observables such as the superconducting order parameter, whose size could be important in future experiments. We provide here the actual calculations for this scenario on the superconducting resonators, calculating the modulation size depending on the dark matter parameters.
item.dc:creator: YeolLin ChoeJo, Yechan Kim, Hye-Sung Lee, Jiheon Lee, Jaeok Yi

item.title: Helical Domain-Wall-Ring Networks Reshape Superconducting Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2606.23599v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Extended domain-wall networks that emerge in moir\'e materials provide a distinct platform for quasi-one-dimensional electronic states. However, the interaction-driven orders in confined networks remain largely unexplored. Here, we discuss superconducting (SC) correlations in interacting helical domain-wall-ring networks in the closed topological domains formed within the moir\'e patterns of an underlying twisted bilayer honeycomb lattice. We first analyze the system within the framework of an infinite-size theory and show that inter-ring SC-pair tunneling is renormalization-group relevant in an appropriate interaction regime, favoring enhanced SC correlations through inter-ring phase locking. To address finite-size effects resulting from the ring-network geometry, we present a self-consistent variational approach. Our analysis shows that even in the regime where the infinite-size theory predicts strongly coupled pair tunneling, the induced phase-locking scale remains strongly suppressed. In contrast, the SC scaling dimension is governed mainly by density-density interactions and ring geometry, decreasing modestly with decreasing twist angle while remaining insensitive to the pair-tunneling strength. This discrepancy demonstrates that ring networks cannot generally be understood as simple finite-size truncations of their infinite-size counterparts but can exhibit qualitatively distinct collective behavior. Our study highlights how the interplay of confinement effects and ring-network geometry can reshape SC correlations.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Chun Hung, Arun Bansil

item.title: Thermal Hall tomography of superconducting topology in rhombohedral graphene
item.description: arXiv:2608.12586v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Chiral superconductors should carry Majorana modes along their edges, yet three decades of work on candidate materials have not measured the integer that counts them. Rhombohedral graphene offers a new route, because its superconductivity coexists with magnetic domains that can be imaged and rewritten. Here we show how heat transport can read this integer and test it against the domain pattern. Warping and finite pair momentum can close the excitation gap while the band Chern number stays fixed. An exact two-band thermal kernel shows how quantization is then lost and bounds the plateau error when the gap survives. Real-space calculations with disorder show that the integer survives disorder several times larger than the gap, because a mobility gap remains. Bogoliubov pockets instead turn the bulk into a heat conductor, and disorder does not restore quantization. Time-reversed domains should show opposite plateaux, and with ideal contacts a wall between them should carry twice either plateau. In microscopic calculations, a written wall carries this number of Majorana channels even when its core is metallic. Writing, moving and erasing such walls would test superconducting topology, its link to magnetism, and protected heat flow in one device.
item.dc:creator: Kumar Ghosh
